evals.name: start-is-default-action
evals.expected_output: Routes to the default `start` action: runs lane-launcher.sh, which resolves the lane config (--config, else $HARNESS_OPS_LANES_CONFIG, else <repo>/.work/lanes/lanes.json, falling back to the pre-move <repo>/.work/lanes.json under a deprecation warning), pulls the repo and refreshes the plugin marketplace, then launches each configured lane NOT already running as a named background session (claude --bg -n <lane> --permission-mode auto [--model] [--effort] <prompt-file-contents>). Prints the script output verbatim.
expectations: Output routes to the start action (lane-launcher.sh with no explicit action), not restart/stop/status
Output reflects that start pulls the repo and updates the plugin marketplace before launching
Output reflects that start launches only lanes not already running (a running lane is skipped), each seeded from its canonical prompt file with its per-lane model/effort
Output does not fabricate lane state — it reflects the config and the live 'claude agents --json' session list

evals.name: restart-stops-then-relaunches
evals.expected_output: Routes to `restart work`: validates 'work' is a configured lane, stops it if running (claude stop <sessionId> resolved from claude agents --json), then relaunches it from its canonical prompt file with its model/effort. Restart discards the running lane's in-flight conversation; start would instead skip an already-running lane.
expectations: Output routes to restart scoped to the named lane, not all lanes
Output reflects stop-then-relaunch (the running session is stopped first via claude stop, then a fresh background session is launched)
Output notes restart always relaunches (unlike start, which skips a running lane)

evals.name: stop-only-touches-configured-lanes
evals.prompt: Will `lanes stop` ever stop a background session I started by hand that is not one of my configured lanes?
evals.expected_output: No. stop (and restart) act on a session ONLY when its name is a lane present in the resolved config. A hand-started session — an unrelated 'PR Babysit', or an interactive window named the same as a lane's ad-hoc twin — is matched by name against the config; names not in the config are never stopped. There is no 'claude agents stop' verb, so stop resolves the sessionId from 'claude agents --json' for a configured lane name only.
expectations: Output states stop only ever targets sessions whose name is a configured lane
Output confirms a session whose name is not in the lane config is never stopped
Output does not claim a 'claude agents stop' verb exists — stop resolves the sessionId from claude agents --json

evals.name: status-is-read-only
evals.expected_output: Routes to `status`: prints a per-lane table (lane, model, effort, running/stopped state, live sessionId) built from the config joined against 'claude agents --json'. It mutates nothing — no pull, no launch, no stop — and flags a lane whose prompt file is missing.
expectations: Output routes to the status action and reports per-lane running/stopped state with the live sessionId
Output reflects that status is read-only (no pull, launch, or stop)
Output reflects that a lane with a missing prompt file is flagged

evals.name: prompt-storage-is-session-local
evals.prompt: Where does the launcher read a lane's canonical prompt from, and is that its permanent home?
evals.expected_output: It reads each lane's prompt from the file named by lanes[].prompt, resolved against prompt_dir (default '.work/lanes', the skill's reserved concern home under the session-local memory root). That home is a sanctioned placement, NOT a durable one: the memory root does not travel between machines, so a fresh machine has no prompts until they are authored there or prompt_dir points at a committed directory. Durable cross-machine prompt storage is outside this skill; the seam is prompt_dir, resolved in one place by resolve_prompt_dir.
expectations: Output identifies prompt_dir (default .work/lanes) as the current, session-local prompt source
Output states the placement is sanctioned but still session-local, and that durable cross-machine prompt storage is outside this skill; the seam is prompt_dir / resolve_prompt_dir
Output does not claim this skill builds or owns durable prompt storage

evals.name: running-lane-cannot-hot-reload-own-fix
evals.prompt: I merged a fix to the babysit skill. My babysit loop lane is still running the old behavior. Will it pick up the fix on its own, or do I have to restart it?
evals.expected_output: It will NOT pick up the fix on its own — a running lane keeps the skill versions it loaded at launch, /loop never re-reads a skill's body on later cycles, and a loop cannot self-trigger /reload-plugins. Restart is the honest refresh mechanism (the same restart that clears context bloat). Detect the unconsumed self-fix with a read-only git probe (default-branch commits touching the plugin path since the lane's launch commit, resolving the default branch rather than assuming main), then `/harness-ops:lanes restart <lane>` at the next cycle boundary to re-pull, refresh the marketplace, and relaunch. See context/refresh.md.
expectations: Output states the running lane will NOT auto-consume the merged fix and explains restart is required

Output attributes this to verified Claude Code behavior (launch-time versions retained, /loop does not re-read the skill body, loop can't self-trigger /reload-plugins) rather than a fixable gap in this skill
Output points to the git staleness probe and `lanes restart` at a cycle boundary as the mechanism
Output does not claim a true mid-session hot-reload of a running loop lane is achievable

evals.name: execution-target-read-from-default-branch
evals.prompt: I edited docs/conventions/execution-target.yaml on my branch to send the work-loop lane to the cloud. If I run `/harness-ops:lanes start` now, does the lane go to the cloud?
evals.expected_output: No. The launcher fetches origin's default branch and reads docs/conventions/execution-target.yaml from that commit with git show, never from the working tree or the current branch, and prints the SHA it read. Until the edit is merged to the default branch, the lane resolves as before. Once merged, the lane's stage (lanes[].stage = work-items:work-loop) selects the skill.work-items.work-loop key. Even then the lane does not go to the cloud: work-loop may read untrusted input (it triages raw intake), and with no deterministic connector and egress check the launcher refuses cloud-session for such a stage. The lane is skipped with an error naming /work-items:attend-queue; it files nothing and does not run locally.
expectations: Output states the unmerged branch edit does not move the lane, because the file is read from origin's default branch after a fetch
Output says the launcher prints the commit SHA it read the file at
Output names the skill.work-items.work-loop key, selected by the lane's stage field
Output states that after the merge the work-loop lane is still refused the cloud because it may read untrusted input, and is skipped rather than run locally

evals.name: untrusted-input-stage-does-not-fall-back
evals.prompt: My triage lane is set to cloud-session, but the Claude GitHub App is not installed on the repo. What does `lanes start` do with it?
evals.expected_output: It does not launch the triage lane to the cloud, and the missing App is not the reason: work-items:triage reads raw intake, which is untrusted input, so the launcher refuses cloud-session for it before any App check and never falls back to a local host. The lane is skipped with an error that names /work-items:attend-queue as the escalation route (nothing is filed), and start exits 1 while the other lanes still launch.
expectations: Output states the triage lane is not launched to the cloud
Output states the triage lane is not launched locally as a fallback, because its input is untrusted
Output names /work-items:attend-queue as the escalation route and does not claim the launcher files an item
Output does not claim installing the Claude GitHub App would let the triage lane run in the cloud

evals.name: scheduled-drain-entry
evals.prompt: I want my `drain` lane (stage work-items:work-loop, effort high) to run every 20 minutes on my Windows laptop without a session open. How do I set that up with lanes, and what happens if a run is still going when the next one is due?
evals.expected_output: Add "schedule": {"every_minutes": 20} to the drain lane in lanes.json and have its prompt file call the work loop with --drain --single-pass. Run `print-schedule --write-script drain`: it writes the lane's script (drain.sh in the scheduled folder of the lanes home), which calls `run-once drain`, and prints a schtasks /Create line (every 20 minutes, /TR running bash on that script) plus its /Delete line; registering it from cmd.exe is the operator's step. Each run-once is one `claude -p` pass in auto mode at the lane's effort, adding --permission-prompts none only when the installed CLI is new enough. A run that is due while another holds the lane's run-once lock exits 0 without running, and Task Scheduler does not start a second instance of a running task.
expectations: Output adds a schedule object with every_minutes 20 to the lane's config
Output uses print-schedule with --write-script and says registering the printed schtasks entry is the operator's step
Output says each scheduled run is a run-once pass using claude -p in auto mode with the lane's effort, not a --bg session
Output says an overlapping run exits without running because the lane's lock is held
Output does not claim the launcher registers the task itself
